title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-01-08

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the Jan 8 1966 Fillmore Acid Test delivers raw early‑Dead blues with decent fidelity despite mic woes, highlighted by a fiery “Death Don't Have No Mercy” and playful National Anthem banter.
ai_review.review: The recording is a historic soundboard tape that, while hampered by occasional microphone problems, remains surprisingly clear for a 1966 source. The performance captures the band in their primal blues phase – Pig Pen’s harpsichord‑ish keys on “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” Jerry’s youthful guitar sparkle, and a raucous rendition of the Star‑Spangled Banner make it a standout early show.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating ≈ 4.2 across 14 reviews, with most reviewers praising the historical value and musical moments; technical complaints are minor compared to overall enthusiasm.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mic issues and occasional drop‑outs noted, but overall clarity is decent for a 1966 tape; listeners find the music easy to hear despite early‑era limitations.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early blues set with Pig Pen front‑and‑center, interspersed with quirky banter and a memorable National Anthem jam; the raw energy builds throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Young Jerry’s guitar on “I’m A Hog For You” described as adorable; his tone noted positively.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s pole‑climbing antics and banter during the National Anthem are highlighted as classic early‑Dead humor.
band_member_comments.Keys: First audible keyboard appears on “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” noted as a historic moment.
